record.question:
A company runs Java applications in Docker containers on self-managed virtual machines and uses a self-managed MySQL database. It wants to migrate to AWS, replace its commercial JDK with a compatible OpenJDK distribution, and stop managing container hosts and database servers. Major application or relational-schema redesign is out of scope. A full database export and import takes six hours, but the allowed cutover outage is 15 minutes.

Which migration approach best meets these requirements?

options.text: Run the containers and MySQL on EC2 instances that mirror the current servers. Replace the commercial JDK with a tested OpenJDK image and manage the hosts as before.

Test Amazon Corretto container images, publish them to ECR, and run the services on ECS with Fargate. Migrate MySQL to a supported RDS for MySQL deployment using DMS full load and change replication, then validate and perform a controlled cutover.
Rewrite the application as Lambda functions and replace MySQL with DynamoDB, redesigning the data access layer around the new key structure.
Run tested Corretto images on ECS with Fargate and migrate MySQL to RDS, but stop the source database for the entire full-data export and import without ongoing change replication.

explanation.text:
<<2>> is correct. This replatforming approach changes the runtime and managed hosting while retaining containers, Java, and MySQL's relational model. Corretto supplies a no-cost OpenJDK distribution. Fargate removes container-host management, RDS manages the database infrastructure, and DMS can transfer existing data while replicating subsequent changes before cutover.

<<1>> can reduce JDK licensing expense but retains the server operations that the company wants to remove.

<<3>> introduces the application and data-model redesign explicitly excluded from scope.

<<4>> selects suitable runtime services but makes the entire data transfer part of the outage, failing the short-cutover requirement for the proposed migration approach.

Validate Java dependencies, container compatibility, supported database versions, schema objects, and data consistency before switching traffic. Change replication reduces the final catch-up window; it does not eliminate cutover coordination or guarantee zero downtime. Replatforming does not mean every configuration remains unchanged.

AWS documentation (checked September 18, 2026): [Amazon Corretto](https://aws.amazon.com/corretto/); [ECS with Fargate](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html); [DMS homogeneous MySQL migration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/dm-migrating-data-mysql.html).

diagram_alt: Replatforming replaces runtime licensing and server operations while preserving the containerized Java and relational application model.

sources.supports: Corretto is a no-cost production-ready OpenJDK distribution compatible with the Java SE standard.
Fargate runs ECS containers without requiring the customer to provision and manage EC2 container hosts.
DMS can migrate MySQL to RDS MySQL with full load and binlog-based change replication before cutover.

editorial_notes: Preserved answer 2. Specified Fargate to substantiate removal of host management and a short-cutover constraint for DMS, and replaced an automatic SQL-to-DynamoDB conversion distractor with an otherwise sound migration that causes prolonged downtime.
